title: Operators: Remainder % by 2
text:
Operators: Remainder % by 2
When we divide two numbers, sometimes the numbers divide evenly
Other times the numbers do not divide evenly
Suppose we share 7 loaves of bread into 2 groups
Then each group gets 3 loaves - that is 3 + 3 === 6
1 loaf is left over, so 3 + 3 + 1 === 7
When we divide two numbers, the left over is called the remainder
So the remainder is 1
When two numbers divide evenly, nothing is left over, so the remainder is 0
% gives the remainder
When we divide by 2, the remainder is always smaller than 2
So if we divide by 2, the remainder is one of these: 0 or 1
0 % 2 is 0
1 % 2 is 1
2 % 2 is 0
3 % 2 is 1
4 % 2 is 0
If the number is even, then the remainder is 0
If the number is odd, then the remainder is 1
The remainder alternates between 0 and 1
Here are some examples:
Remainder expression:
7 % 2
remainder value:
1

text:
Operators: Remainder by dividing %
For 14 / 4 :
14 is the dividend
4 is the divisor
Math.floor(14 / 4) === 3, so the quotient is 3
quotient * divisor

So the whole part is 12
Notice that 4 evenly divides into 12
The divisor (4) always evenly divides into the whole part (12)
However 4 does not evenly divide into 14
The divisor (4) may or may not evenly divide into the dividend (14)
The whole part (12) cannot be larger than the dividend (14)
The whole part (12) is always the largest number, that can be evenly divided by the divisor, that is not larger than the dividend (14)
Now we will subtract the whole part (12) from the dividend (14) to find what is left over:
14 - 12 === 2
So 2 is the remainder
This is the same as 14 % 4 :
14 % 4 === 2
So for 14 % 4
We use this formula: 14 - Math.floor(14 / 4) * 4
And here is the answer: 2
So we know 14 % 4 === 2

Operators: Remainder %
For 14 / 4, remember 14 is the dividend
And Math.floor(14 / 4) * 4 is the whole part
Now we will subtract them from each other:
14 - Math.floor(14 / 4) * 4
This is the same as 14 % 4
So 14 % 4 is 14 - Math.floor(14 / 4) * 4
So the remainder % is the dividend minus its whole part
And this works the same way for any number we divide by
